headline: Fleet cost inflation drives earnings to a loss
summary_short: U-Haul (AMERCO) reported revenue of $1,271.8M, up 3.1% y/y but down 10.2% q/q, while net income swung to a $127.8M loss on higher fleet depreciation, disposal losses, self-insurance costs and interest expense.
summary_long: Full fiscal-year 2026 revenue rose modestly — self-moving equipment rental revenue +$86.4M and self-storage revenue +$74.5M — but earnings fell sharply as total costs and expenses rose $492.7M, driven by $186.6M higher fleet depreciation, $117.6M higher losses on disposal of rental equipment, $76.4M higher self-insured liability costs and higher interest expense ($364.8M vs $295.7M). Earnings from operations dropped $283.5M to $432.6M, and earnings available to common stockholders fell to $83.1M from $367.1M. Cash rose to $1,120.1M as operating cash flow improved $340.2M and investing outflows fell $628.0M. Long-term debt rose to $8,124.9M. For fiscal 2027, management expects to reinvest approximately $815M (net of sales) in the rental fleet, down from $1,381.1M in fiscal 2026.

drivers.explanation: Full-year FY2026 revenue grew on self-moving (+$86.4M) and self-storage (+$74.5M) gains, but higher fleet depreciation, disposal losses, self-insurance costs and interest expense drove earnings sharply lower; the 10-K discusses only full-year, not Q4-isolated, results.

Self-moving equipment rental revenue rose $86.4M and self-storage revenue rose $74.5M for fiscal 2026 vs fiscal 2025, from occupancy gains, new storage capacity, a 5% rise in revenue per occupied foot, and more retail locations/dealers and fleet size.

Full fiscal-year earnings available to common stockholders fell to $83.1M (from $367.1M) as earnings from operations dropped $283.5M on higher depreciation, disposal losses and self-insurance costs, plus higher interest expense, partly offset by lower income tax expense.

Earnings from operations for fiscal 2026 fell $283.5M to $432.6M (from $716.2M) as $186.6M higher fleet depreciation and $117.6M higher disposal losses outpaced modest revenue growth across Moving & Storage.

Diluted EPS fell as full fiscal-year earnings available to common stockholders dropped to $83.1M from $367.1M, driven by higher depreciation, disposal losses, self-insurance costs and interest expense outweighing modest revenue growth.

Debt rose alongside a $168.2M year-over-year increase in borrowings, used with lease and equity financing to help fund the $2,444.0M Moving & Storage fleet and real estate capital program in fiscal 2026.
Operating cash flow rose $340.2M and investing outflows fell $628.0M (real estate spending down $540.6M), more than offsetting a $300.5M decline in cash provided by financing activities.
